q: Is my smart home data in really mine?
a: We help you select hardware and software that doesn't call out to the cloud so your data stays under your control.

Your smart home software runs on a device in your own home (like a small server) instead of a company's cloud. Your automations keep working even if the internet goes down or a vendor shuts off a service.

q: How high is the initial investment?
a: It depends on your property size and type. We offer a variety of services, so a free consultation is the best way to get a realistic picture.

q: Do I need to buy equipment before contacting Cool IoT?
a: No. During the consultation we go over everything that is required, so you only buy what you actually need.

q: Do I need an IT service to maintain my system?
a: No. Everything we use is open source, so you can learn to build your own automations and experiences. Cool IoT is always here to help when you want a hand.
Home Assistant is a free, open-source smart home platform. It connects devices from many brands in one place and runs locally, so your dashboards and automations stay in your home.
ESPHome lets you turn low-cost ESP32/ESP8266 microcontrollers into custom sensors and switches that plug straight into Home Assistant, configured with simple YAML files.
HACS (the Home Assistant Community Store) is a community add-on that makes it easy to install custom integrations, themes and dashboard cards made by other users.

q: How often should I back up my smart home?
a: Automatic backups are best, and at least one copy should live somewhere other than the device running your system. Test restoring a backup occasionally so you know it works.
Z-Wave is a low frequency wireless mesh communication protocol used in smart home devices. It allows secure, long-range and very low-powered communication between devices.
Zigbee is a high frequency wireless mesh communication protocol used in smart home devices. It allows low-powered wireless devices to communicate at reasonably high data rates.

Wi-Fi is a high frequency wireless communication protocol used to connect devices to the internet. It allows devices to communicate at very high data rates, but it uses significantly more power than Z-Wave or Zigbee.
